meta.title: Operation of Digital Plethysmometer in Pharmacology Laboratory

sections.purpose: To accurately measure limb (paw) volume in rodents using the water displacement principle for quantification of oedema formation and anti-inflammatory drug efficacy in carrageenan-induced paw oedema models.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacology laboratory for paw oedema measurement in rodent models of inflammation including carrageenan-induced oedema, dextran-induced oedema, and arthritis models.
procedure: Switch on the digital plethysmometer and allow it to complete initialization.
Fill the measuring cell with distilled water or saline to the marked level — use the same liquid throughout the experiment.
Remove air bubbles from the measuring cell by gently tapping the sides.
Calibrate using the provided calibration cup: immerse fully, and the reading should correspond to the cup volume (e.g., 1.00 mL); adjust if needed.
Press 'Zero' or 'Tare' with the cell empty (just liquid, no object).
Mark the animal's right paw at the tibiotarsal junction using a permanent marker — this ensures consistent immersion depth across all measurements.
Gently lower the marked paw into the measuring cell up to the marked line — hold steadily.
When the reading on the digital display stabilizes, record the baseline paw volume.
Administer the phlogistic agent (e.g., carrageenan 0.1 mL of 1% suspension) by sub-plantar injection into the right hind paw.
Administer the test drug or vehicle by the specified route (oral, i.p.) 30–60 minutes before carrageenan injection.
Measure paw volume at specified time points after carrageenan injection (typically 1, 2, 3, 4 hours).
Calculate % oedema: [(Vt − V₀) / V₀] × 100, where Vt = volume at time t, V₀ = baseline volume.
Calculate % inhibition of oedema: [(Oedema control − Oedema treated) / Oedema control] × 100.
Record all measurements and calculated values in the data sheet.
Clean the measuring cell with distilled water and 70% ethanol between animals.
precautions: Maintain consistent immersion depth — use a permanent marker on the paw at the tibiotarsal junction for every measurement.
Ensure no air bubbles in the measuring cell — air bubbles give falsely low volume readings.
Use the same liquid (distilled water or saline) throughout one experiment — never mix.
Allow the liquid to reach room temperature equilibrium before the first measurement — temperature affects liquid volume.
Handle animals gently — struggling displaces water and gives inaccurate readings.
Calibrate at the start of each experimental session.
Follow CPCSEA and IAEC guidelines for care and use of laboratory animals.
